problems: E27 is a tested-negative result for a significant adipose-subcutaneous eQTL. It weakens an adipose FTO-expression mechanism, but does not by itself contradict the broader claim that FTO is the best-supported target or establish another target.
E25 is explicitly not tested; the lack of a PRRX1 peak there is not evidence against PRRX1 binding. E26 provides RELA occupancy evidence only in aortic endothelial cells, not adipose.

The binding-link wording says the supplied family results do not report which allele binds more, while E12 states that alternate C binds more in vitro. That direction is not assigned to any of the five nominated TFs, so TF-specific allele binding remains unresolved.

The phenotype risk allele is T, whereas E09 reports that alt C increases FTO expression in skeletal muscle. No adipose eQTL is significant (E27), so the gene-expression and disease directions do not establish a coherent adipose mediation mechanism.

checks.why: A variant-overlapping peak in a relevant biosample would strengthen the PRRX1 occupancy link; absence from the queried data would not itself be a tested-negative result.
This directly checks whether the RELA candidate has occupancy evidence at the variant in the relevant context, helping compare it with the other nominated TFs.
An adipose eQTL for this variant could change support for FTO or identify another target in the relevant context.
